title: Threaded eval recap: sampling & fast-probes
content:
Quick stream-of-consciousness summary from sprint afternoons where I tried to squeeze more signal out of small eval budgets. Mostly heuristics, half-formed ideas, and experiment logs. Meant for personal reference and to hand off to Maya/Owen for followups.

Context / goal:
- We have tiny labeled prompt sets for some endpoint regressions (50-200 examples). Want a lightweight strategy to prioritize which prompts to run full-model A/B on and which prompts can be approximated with cheap probes (distilled models, few-shot samplers, or embedding-based reranks).
- Constraints: 2 GPU-hours per day for broad sweeps, need repeatability, noisy metrics (accuracy/fluency/format adherence).

High-level approach (threaded eval idea):
1) Multi-tier probes: cheap -> medium -> heavy. Each prompt moves along pipeline only if probe score uncertainty is high or failure risk flagged.
2) Sampling focus: stratified by prefix length, token-uniqueness (entropy proxy), and historical failure signals (error tags).
3) Bootstrap ensembles: run N=5 cheap perturbations (temperature, few-shot order) and use disagreement as an uncertainty signal to escalate.

Concrete heuristics tried this week (notes + outcomes):
- Heuristic A: sample 20% prompts with longest expected generation length (from prior runs) for heavy run. Outcome: high recall of regressions but costly; recall ~0.85 on the 50-case validation but precision low (many false positives).
- Heuristic B: use embed-distance to a set of 'known hard prompts' (k=10) -> escalate if distance < threshold. Outcome: low false positives, but missed several syntactic-format regressions.
- Heuristic C: disagreement score on 3 cheap sampled decodes (t=0.8, greedy, t=0.3) as escalation trigger. Outcome: best tradeoff so far: captured semantic failures; some format errors slip through.

Notes on cheap probes we used:
- Distilled 3B model (local dev) used as first-tier proxy. Extremely fast, but misses many edge-case hallucinations. Use only to filter out obviously stable prompts.
- Embedding-similarity reranker (Ada-like embed) on top of n-best decodes for medium-tier. Useful for picking model vs golden-output mismatches.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- How to quantify "format correctness" cheaply? Regex heuristics + classifier? Lightweight LM prompt scoring seems plausible but brittle.
- Can we learn a small escalation classifier from a few labeled escalations? I sketched a logistic reg with features: prefix_len, avg_token_entropy (approx), embed_dist_to-hard, disagreement_score. Need ~200 labeled to generalize.
- Should we include latency cost in the priority score? Yes, but how to normalize across models/regions? Need a unit cost metric (tokens/sec normalized by model size + queueing).

Planned experiments (next short sprint):
- E1: Train binary escalation classifier using historical 280 labeled prompts (label = required heavy run). Split 70/30, k-fold. Quick feature ablation. Target: precision >= 0.7 at recall >= 0.6. (Assign to Maya)
- E2: Implement tiny format-checker based on sequence-labeler probe (fast single-token classifier) and evaluate on known format-fail set (Owen).
- E3: Compare stratified sampling (length+entropy) vs pure uncertainty (disagreement) on cost-vs-detected-regressions curve. Need deterministic seeds and fixed probe budget.

Quick mini-results log (timestamped):
- 2024-11-08 15:10 — ran a 2h sweep of Heuristic C on 120 prompts, budget hit 1.8 GPU-hrs, found 9 regressions; manual triage says 7 are meaningful.
- 2024-11-09 09:05 — embed-distance filter removed 40% of prompts; among removals, 2 were actual regressions -> false negatives.

Implementation notes / snippets to copy into scripts: 
- disagreement_score = variance(logprobs across decodes) / mean(abs(lengths - expected_length) + 1)  # crude but correlates
- embed_dist_to_hard = min_cosine(my_prompt_embed, hard_set_embeds)

Things to document for handoff:
- Data schema for escalation training set (prompt_id, prefix_len, expected_tokens, cheap_probe_outputs (n), disagreement_score, embed_dist_min, label_escalate) — we should store as CSV in repro-playground.
- Repro steps for cheap probe env: docker image tag = redwood/dev-probe:v0.3, weights in s3://redwood-dev/dists/3b-v1/

Links / further reading I kept in a tab: 
- self-consistency & majority-vote papers (arxiv links in linked_artifacts) — useful for ensemble disagreement framing.
- short blog on "active sampling for evaluation" (pseudocode inspiration).

Quick personal takeaways: 
- Cheap ensemble disagreement is a surprisingly strong signal for semantic errors; format errors need specialized detectors.
- Embedding filters help reduce cost but can be blind to orthogonal failure modes; combine signals.
- We need a small labeled training set for escalation classifier — low-effort labeling during manual triage is feasible and will pay off quickly.

TODOs to myself: 
- [ ] Wire up JIRA-REPRO-412 with the new CSV export.
- [ ] Sketch UI for "escalation preview" in Console so SREs can see which prompts were auto-escalated.
- [ ] Run E1 training draft and post results to shared slack #eval-puppeteers.

Random notes: 
- Found a neat idea: sample perturbations by swapping few-shot exemplar order (rather than content) — cheap and can expose brittleness in in-context learning usage. Worth trying as part of disagreement ensemble.
- Consider using prefix-substitution (synonym swap) to detect lexical brittleness — cheap token-level edit + probe.

If anyone (Maya/Owen) wants to pick up experiments E1/E2, ping me and I'll drop the CSV dump and the minimal pipeline scripts in repro-playground.

End of stream.
